speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in relation to the Zero Waste Masterplan’s target of achieving an overall recycling rate of 70% by 2030 (a) what is the breakdown of our recycling rate targets by waste type; (b) what is the target recycling rate for plastics; and (c) what are the pathways to raising the plastic recycling rate from 6% today to the intended 2030 target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In a resource- and carbon-constrained world, recycling enables us to reduce emissions and achieve a circular economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are focusing efforts on three priority waste streams, namely, packaging waste, including plastics, electronic waste and food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Plastics are generated in large quantities, but the recycling rate is low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have various initiatives to drive plastics recycling on both the domestic and industrial fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The National Recycling Programme caters to residential premises, while the Mandatory Packaging Reporting scheme encourages companies to reduce the amount of packaging they use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Under this scheme, large producers of packaged products and retailers must report the amount of packaging they introduce into Singapore annually and develop 3R – or reduce, reuse, recycle – plans for packaging materials, including plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Agencies are also exploring innovative solutions with the private sector that will allow us to recycle more plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will need everyone's collective efforts to reduce, reuse and recycle, in order to achieve our national recycling rate target.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I am not sure I caught the answer to the question in the original Parliamentary Question (PQ), in terms of the target —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Chua, could I invite you to speak up please, or speak into the microphone?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Specific to the original PQ that I asked on the recycling rates by category, I asked that because if you look at the plastics, for example, it is only about 6%; whereas for categories, such as ferrous metal, it is already at 99%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, in terms of getting to the 2030 target recycling rate, what would be the breakdown for some of these targets?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: Specifically, for plastics, given that there have been studies which indicate that it is technically feasible to undertake chemical recycling here in Singapore, what are the plans around this in terms of implementation?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, I must clarify that I am answering the Member's question because there is only one question; there is no amended question.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Member is right to say that, in the case of certain waste streams like ferrous metals, or construction and demolition waste, for instance, we have successfully achieved close to 100% recycling rate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted earlier, we have identified and are focusing on three priority waste streams – which are the packaging waste, that includes plastic; e-waste; as well as food waste – because these are generated in large volumes and we expect these volumes to likely increase, for instance, electrical and electronic waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we are focusing and targeting on these.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They are large volumes, but the recycling rate, as the Member has also rightly pointed out, is low.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we do track and publish these recycling rates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we also recognise that for certain waste streams, they are interconnected.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, when we implement the beverage container return scheme, which will cover plastic bottles as well as metal cans, the recycling rate for these used beverage containers will increase and is likely to reduce the contamination rate in our blue recycling bins or the recycling chutes; which means that the recycling rates for the other waste streams in the recycling bins or recycling chutes would increase.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And that is why we think that by having an overall recycling rate target, it provides us with a streamlined approach to track the progress we are making in terms of achieving our vision of a zero-waste nation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding that, even though we do not have specific targets for certain waste streams, when we implement initiatives to drive the recycling rates for various waste streams – for instance, e-waste – we, actually, do set targets under the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When we implement an EPR for packaging waste, which we are planning to do, we will also similarly set targets for this.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We shall move on to Mr Lim Biow Chuan.
